title: Container Bookings: Empty Equipment Release and Shipment Milestones
content:
Between confirmation and departure a Container Bookings booking passes through the release of empty equipment and then through gate-in, loading, departure and closure. This page states the release conditions and who records each milestone.

## Release of empty equipment

Empties are released against a confirmed booking when the customer asks for them, subject to all of the following, each read from the line's records:

- **Timing.** Release happens no earlier than the product's release period, in calendar days, ahead of the scheduled departure date. The first permissible release date is that departure date moved back by that number of whole calendar days, and a release on that date itself is allowed.
- **Prepayment.** Where the customer's credit standing is cash in advance and the product requires prepayment before release, the booking's outstanding charges must stand at 0.00 before release. Customers whose credit standing is credit approved are never held back for prepayment.
- **Dangerous goods.** A booking whose cargo category is dangerous goods is released only once its dangerous-goods acceptance is approved.
- **Reefer.** A booking whose cargo category is reefer is released only once its reefer service has passed pre-trip inspection.

**Short equipment.** If the depot is short of the 40DV booked and the product allows free substitution, a 40HC is released at no additional charge. In any other case the customer either waits until the booked type is available or changes the equipment type under the amendment rules, except that a product with guaranteed equipment never leaves the customer waiting.

**Effect.** Release moves the booking from confirmed to equipment released and opens the booking's export free-time record under the demurrage and detention rules.

## Later milestones

The four later milestones are entered by the terminal and vessel systems alone; the desk has no power to set any of them. A container is loaded only once its VGM has been received. When a booking rated under a service contract departs, its volume is credited to that contract as lifted volume under the contract rules.

| Milestone | Status reached | Recorded by |
|---|---|---|
| Laden containers received at the load terminal | gated in | terminal system |
| Containers on board the allocated vessel | loaded | vessel system |
| Vessel leaves the port of loading | departed | vessel system |
| Discharge and file closure | closed | system |

## Release window boundary (hypothetical)

With a scheduled departure on day D and a release period of 10 days, the earliest release date is day D less ten. Releasing on that day is allowed; releasing on day D less eleven is not. The dates and period are invented.
